To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed a robust and efficient Bayesian parameter-estimation algorithm, and have demonstrated that it can recover the intrinsic source parameters of a compact-binary inspiral signal embedded in real LIGO data.

we can estimate the chirp mass of the binary with 1.3 per cent accuracy and the symmetric mass ratio with 8 per cent accuracy using the non-spinning wave forms, and 1.2 per cent accuracy and 2.0 per cent accuracy using spinning wave forms.

the accuracy with which the physical parameters of a compact binary inspiral can be estimated is of order a few per cent for non-spinning wave forms, and that the bias between the injected parameters and those recovered from the data is of order a per cent for non-precessing wave forms, and of order a few tens of a per cent for precessing wave forms.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of the techniques required for the extraction of physical parameters from the gravitational-wave signal emitted by coalescences of compact binary systems, and their implementation in the analysis of real LIGO data.
the analysis of gravitational-wave data from the LIGO detector and the development of a Bayesian approach to the analysis of gravitational waveforms from coalescing compact binaries.
the development of the parameter estimation technique for gravitational-wave signals, which will be crucial for the analysis of the data from advanced gravitational wave detectors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the accuracy of the parameter estimates is limited by the accuracy of the waveforms.
the injected signals were recovered with a good accuracy and the analysis technique is ready for the detection of gravitational waves from compact binary inspiral.
the injected waveforms are consistent with the recovered ones, and that the parameter-estimation technique works well in real data.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in the absence of a spin prior, the spin parameters are not well-constrained by a single LIGO observation.
, with the current sensitivity of LIGO, we can measure the masses of coalescing compact binary systems with a precision of better than 10% and the symmetric mass ratio with a precision of 0.05–0.2.

the accuracy of the parameter estimation for the injected signals was comparable to that of the injected signals, but the bias in the recovered parameters is significant and needs to be addressed in future work.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the accuracy of the recovered parameter is not affected much by the spin of the binary components, and is dominated by the post-Newtonion order of the waveform used in analysis.
the accuracy of the estimated parameters is limited by the available waveform templates.
the Bayesian approach can be used to determine the physical properties of compact binary inspirals, even in the presence of noise.
